facts.project_name: Synagogue & Community House — Energy Conservation Measures Program
facts.notes: Concept level estimate only. Two existing occupied buildings totaling approximately 100,000 GSF. ECM scope narrative is the only design information provided; an FCA exists and is referenced but was not provided.

deliverables.name: Concept Level Estimate — Energy Conservation Measures
deliverables.description: Order-of-magnitude construction cost estimate covering all listed ECMs across both buildings, including Option 1 / Option 2 comparative pricing of the steam-to-hot-water conversion and the triple-pane window alternate; one estimate review meeting with the Owner and design team; incorporation of one consolidated round of comments; final issue.
deliverables.source_language: proposal is for concept level estimate only

gaps.question: No drawings, FCA report, equipment schedules, or existing-conditions documentation were provided.
gaps.why_it_matters: Concept accuracy and estimating effort both depend on what can be measured versus what must be carried as allowance.
gaps.proposed_assumption: The estimate will be prepared from the ECM scope narrative, one site walk, and gross-square-foot benchmarks; the FCA report and any available drawings will be made available at kickoff.
gaps.pricing_basis: Concept (ROM) level estimate in Uniformat, allowance-based quantities on 100,000 GSF total

gaps.question: The split of the 100,000 SF between the Synagogue and Community House, and the floor count of each building, are not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Per-floor measures (fan coils, VAV dampers, lighting, wall insulation) scale directly with floor count.
gaps.proposed_assumption: Building areas and floor counts will be confirmed at the site walk; quantities are pro-rated on 100,000 GSF total pending confirmation.
gaps.pricing_basis: Per-floor quantities per the scope narrative, e.g. (6) perimeter fan coils per floor at 1 ton / 400 cfm

gaps.question: Whether Option 1 and Option 2 for the steam-to-hot-water conversion are both to be fully priced is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Carrying two full mechanical options materially increases estimating effort.
gaps.proposed_assumption: The base estimate carries Option 2 (conversion at each building), with Option 1 (central conversion with street crossing) priced at concept level and presented as a comparative cost delta.
gaps.pricing_basis: One base estimate plus one option delta summary

gaps.question: Permitting requirements, utility interferences, and restoration requirements for the street excavation are unknown.
gaps.why_it_matters: Street work is the stated cost driver separating Option 1 from Option 2 and carries high variability.
gaps.proposed_assumption: Street excavation, backfill, pavement restoration, and permitting for Option 1 are carried as an allowance assuming a single trench crossing; no utility relocations are assumed.
gaps.pricing_basis: Single trench crossing allowance; utility test pits and investigations excluded

gaps.question: The number of unrenovated floors to receive the LED upgrade is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: The per-floor fixture counts are given, but the floor count multiplies them.
gaps.proposed_assumption: The lighting and plug-load upgrade is priced on the per-floor fixture counts in the scope, applied to all floors not yet renovated to the 5th Floor standard; the floor count will be confirmed at the site walk.
gaps.pricing_basis: Approximately (30) 2x2 LED and (16) 5-inch recessed LED fixtures per floor, plus occupancy-based receptacle controls

gaps.question: Construction phasing and whether work must occur off-hours in occupied spaces is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Off-hours labor premiums materially move mechanical and electrical costs in occupied buildings.
gaps.proposed_assumption: Both buildings are assumed occupied during construction; an off-hours work premium is carried as a percentage allowance on trades working in occupied areas.
gaps.pricing_basis: Percentage premium allowance on affected mechanical and electrical trades

gaps.question: No hazardous materials survey was provided; steam piping insulation and existing wall finishes are typical asbestos-containing suspects in buildings of this vintage.
gaps.why_it_matters: Abatement can swing demolition and piping conversion costs significantly.
gaps.proposed_assumption: An abatement allowance is carried as a separately identified line; hazardous materials survey and abatement design are excluded.
gaps.pricing_basis: Identified abatement allowance only, quantity unverified

gaps.question: The anticipated construction start and duration are not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Escalation to the construction midpoint is a visible line in any concept estimate and needs a schedule basis.
gaps.proposed_assumption: The estimate is prepared in current-day dollars with escalation shown as a separately identified line to an assumed construction midpoint approximately 18 months from estimate issue.
gaps.pricing_basis: Escalation percentage applied as an identified line on the estimate summary

gaps.question: Whether the estimate review is in person or virtual is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: On-site presentation adds travel time for senior staff.
gaps.proposed_assumption: One estimate review meeting is included, held virtually; an on-site presentation can be provided as an additional service at the hourly rates herein.
gaps.pricing_basis: One 2-hour virtual review meeting including preparation

gaps.question: The number of comment/revision rounds on the estimate is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Each additional revision cycle adds assembly and review hours.
gaps.proposed_assumption: One consolidated round of review comments is incorporated in the final issue; further revisions or re-issues will be billed at the hourly rates herein.

gaps.question: Which floors will be renovated (triggering the wall insulation measure), and when, is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: The measure is defined per renovated floor; its quantity is otherwise open-ended.
gaps.proposed_assumption: Wall insulation is priced on a per-floor unit basis for the same floors assumed for the lighting upgrade, as future-renovation scope.
gaps.pricing_basis: 2-inch mineral wool at exterior walls including finish removal and replacement, per-floor unit basis

gaps.question: The Community House window count is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Window replacement is priced per unit; the count is the estimate.
gaps.proposed_assumption: The window count will be estimated from facade observation at the site walk; the base carries double-pane IGU with the triple-pane unit priced as an add alternate.
gaps.pricing_basis: Unit cost per window opening, count to be confirmed

exclusions_suggested: Energy modeling, savings/payback analysis, and measurement & verification
Life cycle cost analysis / OPEX costing
Value engineering beyond the Option 1 / Option 2 comparison described
Additional estimates or milestones beyond those listed
Hazardous materials survey and abatement design
Estimating lengthy or significant design revisions after receipt of documents and notice to proceed
Reimbursables (billed at cost with no markup, if incurred)
